requirements.title: CLOSE terminates the connection of a specified unit to an external file
requirements.definition: The CLOSE statement is the input/output statement used to terminate the connection of a specified unit to an external file.

pending.close-terminates-specified-unit-connecti: Open a controlled named external file on a selected unit, establish OPENED=.true. by INQUIRE into a logical initialized to the opposite value, execute CLOSE, then INQUIRE that same unit into a nondefault logical and expect OPENED=.false.; the pre-open inquiry prevents a vacuous already-closed result.

requirements.title: A CLOSE may be executed from any program unit and need not match the OPEN program unit
requirements.definition: Execution of a CLOSE statement for a unit may occur in any program unit and is not required to occur in the same program unit as the OPEN for that unit.

pending.close-any-program-unit-permitted: Open a known file in the main program, call a contained or module procedure that executes CLOSE on the passed unit, and then INQUIRE from the caller that the unit is closed; the file is first opened to make the close effect non-vacuous.
pending.close-open-program-unit-match-not-requir: Use distinct OPEN and CLOSE procedure bodies with an already-open unit and verify by post-CLOSE INQUIRE that matching program units were not required.

requirements.title: CLOSE waits for pending asynchronous transfers on the unit
requirements.definition: Execution of a CLOSE statement performs a wait operation for any pending asynchronous data transfer operations for the specified unit.

pending.close-waits-for-pending-asynchronous-tra: After asynchronous data transfer support is registered, start a pending transfer on a controlled unit with an ID initialized to a nondefault value, execute CLOSE, and observe completion through the portable WAIT/IOSTAT status relation; no timing or buffering assumption is used.

requirements.title: Closing a nonexistent, unconnected, or no-file unit is permitted and has no effect
requirements.definition: Execution of CLOSE for a unit that does not exist, is connected to a nonexistent file, or has no file connected to it is permitted and affects no file or unit.

pending.close-nonexistent-unit-permitted: Guarded positive plan: probe candidate unit numbers with INQUIRE(UNIT=u, EXIST=e) into a logical prefilled .true.; only when a probe assigns e=.false. does the fixture exercise this facet. For such a unit, execute CLOSE(UNIT=u, IOSTAT=stat) with stat initialized to a nonzero sentinel, require stat==0, then repeat INQUIRE(UNIT=u, EXIST=e) into a .true.-prefilled logical and require e=.false. again. If every probed unit reports EXIST=.true., this facet is not exercised because the standard does not guarantee any particular unit number is nonexistent; do not substitute OPENED=.false., which belongs to the unconnected-unit facet.
pending.close-unconnected-unit-permitted: First establish by INQUIRE that a valid unit number is not connected, execute CLOSE on it, and verify the unit remains not open; the pre-inquiry avoids passing because it was never tested.
pending.close-no-file-no-effect: Create a separate control file with known existence, close an unrelated unconnected unit, and verify the control file still exists; no assertion is made about processor file names.

requirements.title: A disconnected unit may be connected again in the same program
requirements.definition: After a unit has been disconnected by CLOSE, it may be connected again within the same program to the same file or to a different file.

pending.unit-reconnect-same-file-permitted: Open a named file, write distinct content, CLOSE with KEEP, reopen the same unit to the same file, and read the content into a sentinel variable; the prior close and known content make the reconnection observable.
pending.unit-reconnect-different-file-permitted: Open and close a first controlled file, then reopen the same unit to a second controlled file with different known content and read it into a sentinel variable; the differing content distinguishes the target.

requirements.title: A disconnected named file may be connected again if it still exists
requirements.definition: After a named file has been disconnected by CLOSE, it may be connected again within the same program to the same or a different unit, provided that the file still exists.

pending.named-file-reconnect-same-unit-if-exists: Close a named file with KEEP after writing known content, reopen it on the same unit, and read the content into a nondefault sentinel; existence is established by successful read rather than assumed.
pending.named-file-reconnect-different-unit-if-e: Close a named file with KEEP, reopen the same file on a different unused unit, and read known content; the two unit numbers are inquired before use to avoid accidental preconnection.

requirements.title: Normal termination closes connected nonscratch units with KEEP status
requirements.definition: During normal termination completion, every connected unit whose prior file status is not SCRATCH is closed with status KEEP.

pending.normal-termination-closes-connected-nons: Run a helper program that opens a named nonscratch file, writes known content, leaves the unit connected, and terminates normally; a separate driver then opens the known file and reads the content into sentinels. The file is created before termination so survival is non-vacuous.
pending.normal-termination-nonscratch-default-ke: Use the same normal-termination helper without an explicit CLOSE, and verify the named nonscratch file remains; no processor-dependent default is asserted for this scoped CLOSE rule.

requirements.title: Normal termination closes connected scratch units with DELETE status
requirements.definition: During normal termination completion, every connected unit whose prior file status is SCRATCH is closed with status DELETE.

pending.normal-termination-closes-connected-scra: No portable oracle exists for the DELETE disposition performed at normal termination for a connected SCRATCH file. A helper can open a scratch file and write known content before normal termination, but after termination the unit is gone and the scratch file has no portable FILE= name for an EXIST= inquiry; observing only pre-termination OPENED state or helper exit would not observe deletion.
pending.normal-termination-scratch-default-delet: No portable oracle exists for the default DELETE disposition at normal termination for a SCRATCH file. The program cannot execute an inquiry after its own normal-termination completion, and an external driver has no standard-conforming pathname or unit handle for the scratch file; named-file DELETE or nonscratch KEEP have portable FILE= EXIST= oracles, but this scratch case does not.

Mixed permission/no-effect source unit split into fine units.
Permission to execute CLOSE for nonexistent, no-file, or unconnected unit cases.
Reconnect permissions for units and named files are split.
Permission to reconnect a disconnected unit.
Permission to reconnect a named file only when it still exists.

NOTE describes the effect by analogy to CLOSE without STATUS=; it is not an independent normative requirement.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.5.7-12.6.1, the CLOSE statement and data transfer statements in general (batch152). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across three rounds. Round 1 found a conditional KEEP-on-nonexistent-file plan and scratch DELETE plans that observed only unit closure; both are now explicit no-portable-oracle reasons (no portable way to connect a nonexistent file with KEEP allowed; no portable name for a scratch file), while named-file DELETE keeps a portable EXIST= plan established before the CLOSE. Round 2 found the nonexistent-unit CLOSE plan relied on OPENED=.false.; it is now guarded on INQUIRE EXIST=.false., since no unit number is guaranteed nonexistent. The eight numbered rules were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
